ai.title: deepseek-reasoner added to lite agent
ai.summary: deepseek-reasoner replaces deepseek-chat for --lite agent via main-prompt.ts. Uses DeepSeek beta endpoint for prefix prompts; omits temperature for reasoner. Cost tracking updated in message-cost-tracker.ts. Model constant added to common/src/constants.ts.

eli5.text: If you run the assistant in its lightweight mode, it will now think through your request more carefully before answering, instead of responding quickly. The new model it uses is better at reasoning but costs a bit more per question than the one it replaced. You wouldn't see any buttons change, but answers in that mode may take slightly longer to appear while the assistant works through more steps. The price tracking was also updated so the cost of these heavier answers is measured correctly. The change is live today for anyone using the lightweight mode.

ai.title: Update local development setup instructions
ai.summary: README.md now mandates sequential package builds (common, code-map, npm-app) before root dependency installation. npm-app/knowledge.md adds required stack.env and .env.local configuration templates for local execution.

eli5.text: The guide for getting the project running on your own computer now requires you to build three parts in a specific order before installing the main dependencies, and it includes new template files you must copy into place for the app to find its settings. If you try to follow the old instructions, the setup will fail because the helper files won't exist yet.

ai.title: Add analyze-overages script for Stripe billing
ai.summary: New `scripts/analyze-overages.ts` utility aggregates Stripe billing data to calculate customer overages. It iterates active subscriptions, checks tiered pricing on recent invoices, and computes overage amounts by comparing usage against base tier limits. The script outputs per-plan statistics, including total overage revenue, average overage per customer, and usage distribution buckets ($0-$50, $50-$100, $100+).

eli5.text: A new internal tool was added that scans Stripe billing data to find customers who went over their plan's included usage and calculate how much extra revenue that overage generated. It only looks at active subscribers with at least two paid invoices, identifies tiered pricing items on the most recent invoice, and compares usage against the first pricing tier to compute overage amounts. The script then groups these overages by plan and prints per-plan summaries including total overage revenue, average overage per customer, and usage distribution buckets ($0-$50, $50-$100, $100+). This is behind-the-scenes housekeeping for internal analysis, not a change to what subscribers experience when billing.

ai.title: System prompt warns against unrequested npm install
ai.summary: Updated `backend/src/system-prompt.ts` to explicitly caution against running `npm install` without user permission, directing the agent to check knowledge files for project-specific package manager instructions (e.g., pnpm, bun, yarn, pip). This change mitigates the risk of agents modifying `node_modules` or `package.json` unexpectedly. The scope is limited to the backend system prompt definition.

eli5.text: The assistant was told to be more careful before installing new tools automatically. Now, before it runs a command to add new software packages, it has to pause and check the project's setup notes first, and it needs to get your okay before doing it. This change is already live for the internal system that controls how the assistant behaves, and it only affects projects where that system prompt is being used.

ai.title: Support read-only ~/.knowledge.md user files
ai.summary: Agent injects `~/.knowledge.md` files from user home into system prompt context. `ProjectFileContextSchema` adds optional `userKnowledgeFiles` field; `npm-app/src/project-files.ts` scans `os.homedir()` for `*knowledge.md` files via `findKnowledgeFilesInDir`. Backend `system-prompt.ts` marks these files read-only, forbidding `<edit_file>` blocks; `main-prompt.ts` and `getResponseFormatPrompt` update `hasKnowledgeFiles` checks to include user files. Scope: `backend/src/main-prompt.ts`, `backend/src/system-prompt.ts`, `common/src/util/file.ts`, `npm-app/src/project-files.ts`.

eli5.text: The assistant can now look at personal note files (like ~/.knowledge.md) that you keep in your home folder to better understand your preferences and project context. When those files appear, the system treats them as read-only, it won't try to edit or move them, since they live outside your project folder. You’ll only notice this if you already had one of those note files, and they must still exist for anything to change today; without such a file in place, nothing happens yet.
